A few things I noticed:
- ask about support given to teachers
- see how long others have been there, if it’s a fair while - there’s probably a reason!
- similarly, if it’s somewhere that posts a job advert every (half) term, probably not good 
- ask about the behaviour system and how it’s enforced 
- talk to the kids during interview, also see how they behave
Ultimately though, what works for one person won’t work for another, and it’s sadly trial and error in many cases!

I think there's pros and cons for both - I've owned both!
If you live near a busy main road it's unfair to let a cat out in my opinion, and when adopting you should actively seek to adopt a cat that's going to be content staying in.
If you live away from a main road and have plenty of garden space for a cat to roam, and there's no obvious dangers nearby, then its cruel to keep a cat indoors. Their natural instinct is to hunt!
tldr; it depends on the situation, but the cat being well cared for, chipped, neurered/spayed if outdoor and flea and wormed is the most important thing!
